back: Blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit: pulmonary (to lungs) and systemic (to body).
Thick; tunica media with elastic fibres and smooth muscle; collagen outer layer; withstands and smooths high pressure.
Thin wall, wide lumen, valves; blood at low pressure helped by skeletal muscle.
Wall of endothelium only, lumen about 7-10 µm; short diffusion distance; leaky for tissue fluid.
Neutrophil: lobed nucleus. Monocyte: kidney-shaped nucleus, largest. Lymphocyte: large round nucleus.
Fluid around cells formed from plasma forced out of capillaries by hydrostatic pressure; lacks cells and most plasma proteins.
Venous end: lower hydrostatic pressure, plasma proteins lower blood ψ, water returns by osmosis; excess becomes lymph.

front: Which vessel carries oxygenated blood to the heart?

back: Water (plasma is about 90% water): solvent and carrier of heat.
